stem: The period of life when the body undergoes changes leading to reproductive maturity is called __________.
solution: Adolescence is the period of growth and change from about 11 to 18 or 19 years, leading to reproductive maturity.

stem: Adolescence generally begins around the age of __________ years.
solution: Adolescence typically begins around 11 years of age and continues up to about 18–19 years.

stem: The time at which the reproductive organs become functional and the body becomes capable of reproduction is called __________.
solution: Puberty is the stage during adolescence when the reproductive organs mature and become functional.

stem: A sudden increase in height during adolescence is due to the __________.
options: lengthening of the long bones of the arms and legs
solution: The growth spurt in adolescence is mainly due to the lengthening of the long bones of the arms and legs.

stem: The chemical substances that control the changes at adolescence are called __________.
solution: Hormones, secreted by endocrine glands, control the changes during adolescence.

stem: The glands that secrete hormones directly into the blood are called __________ glands.
solution: Endocrine glands are ductless glands that release hormones directly into the bloodstream.

stem: The male sex hormone is __________.
solution: Testosterone, secreted by the testes, is the male sex hormone that controls male changes at puberty.

stem: The female sex hormone is __________.
solution: Oestrogen, secreted by the ovaries, is the female sex hormone controlling female changes at puberty.

stem: The gland that controls other endocrine glands and is called the 'master gland' is the __________.
solution: The pituitary gland regulates the secretions of other endocrine glands, so it is called the master gland.

stem: The features that help distinguish a mature male from a mature female (like facial hair or development of breasts) are called __________.
solution: Secondary sexual characters, like facial hair in males and breast development in females, distinguish mature males from females.

stem: In boys at puberty, one of the changes is the __________.
options: development of facial hair and deepening of the voice
solution: In boys, puberty brings facial hair, a deeper voice and broadening of the shoulders.

stem: In girls at puberty, one of the changes is the __________.
options: development of breasts and onset of menstruation
cracking of the voice into a deep tone
solution: In girls, puberty brings breast development, widening of the hips, and the onset of menstruation.

stem: The voice of boys deepens at puberty because of the growth of the __________.
solution: The larynx (voice box) grows larger in boys, producing the deeper adult voice; 'Adam's apple' becomes prominent.

stem: The monthly release of an egg and the breakdown and shedding of the uterus lining in females is called __________.
solution: Menstruation is the monthly cycle in which the uterus lining is shed if the egg is not fertilised.

stem: The first menstruation in a girl, marking the start of the reproductive phase, is called __________.
solution: Menarche is the onset of the first menstruation in a girl.

stem: The permanent stopping of menstruation in a woman, usually around 45–50 years, is called __________.
solution: Menopause is the permanent cessation of menstruation, usually between 45 and 50 years of age.

stem: The sex of a baby is determined by __________.
options: the type of chromosomes inherited from the parents
solution: Sex is determined by sex chromosomes: XX gives a girl and XY gives a boy.

stem: Humans have __________ pairs of chromosomes in their cells.
solution: Human cells have 23 pairs (46 chromosomes), one pair being the sex chromosomes.

stem: A baby girl is born when the sex chromosomes are __________.
solution: A girl (XX) results when the father contributes an X chromosome; a boy (XY) when he contributes a Y.

stem: Which chromosome from the father determines that the baby will be a boy?
solution: If the father's sperm carries a Y chromosome (XY), the baby is a boy; if it carries X (XX), a girl.

stem: It is scientifically WRONG to blame the mother for the sex of the child because __________.
options: the sex of the baby is determined by the father's chromosome
sex is random and unrelated to chromosomes
solution: The mother always contributes an X chromosome; the father's sperm (X or Y) determines the sex, so blaming the mother is unscientific and wrong.

stem: The gland that secretes thyroxine and can cause goitre if it lacks iodine is the __________.
solution: The thyroid gland secretes thyroxine; iodine deficiency causes goitre (swelling of this gland).

stem: The pancreas secretes the hormone __________, which controls blood sugar.
solution: Insulin from the pancreas regulates blood sugar; its deficiency causes diabetes.

stem: The deficiency of insulin causes the disease __________.
solution: A deficiency of insulin causes diabetes, marked by high blood sugar levels.

stem: The 'emergency hormone' adrenaline is secreted by the __________ glands.
solution: The adrenal glands secrete adrenaline, which prepares the body to respond to stress or danger.

stem: A balanced diet is especially important during adolescence because __________.
options: the body is growing rapidly and needs more nutrients
solution: Rapid growth during adolescence increases the need for a balanced, nutritious diet.

stem: Iron-rich foods are important for adolescents, especially girls, to prevent __________.
solution: Iron helps form haemoglobin; a shortage causes anaemia, a common concern for adolescent girls.

stem: Personal hygiene during adolescence is important because __________.
options: increased sweat and oil secretion can cause body odour and skin problems
solution: Active sweat and oil glands during adolescence make regular bathing and hygiene important to avoid odour and skin problems like acne.

stem: Adolescents should avoid drugs, alcohol and tobacco because these __________.
options: harm health and can lead to addiction
solution: Drugs, alcohol and tobacco damage health and can cause addiction, so adolescents must avoid them.

stem: The pimples and acne that appear during adolescence are caused by increased secretion from __________.
solution: Increased activity of sebaceous (oil) glands during adolescence often causes acne and pimples.

stem: AIDS is a disease that can be transmitted from an infected person to a healthy person through __________.
options: infected blood, sharing needles, or from mother to baby
solution: HIV/AIDS spreads through infected blood, unsafe needles, and from mother to child, not by casual contact.

stem: Reproductive health means being __________.
options: physically and mentally healthy with respect to reproductive life
solution: Reproductive health refers to total well-being (physical and mental) related to reproduction.

stem: The hormones released by the testes and ovaries at puberty are triggered by a hormone from the __________.
solution: The pituitary gland releases hormones that stimulate the testes and ovaries to produce sex hormones.

stem: During adolescence, the body changes are mostly __________.
options: controlled by hormones and are a normal part of growing up
solution: The changes at adolescence are normal, hormone-controlled and a natural part of maturing.

stem: Which of the following is a secondary sexual character in males?
options: Growth of a beard and moustache
solution: Facial hair (beard and moustache) is a secondary sexual character in males.

stem: Which of the following is a secondary sexual character in females?
options: Deepening of the voice into a bass tone
solution: Breast development is a secondary sexual character in females.

stem: The menstrual cycle in a woman is typically about __________ days long.
solution: The menstrual cycle is about 28 days on average.

stem: The endocrine glands are also called __________ glands.
solution: Endocrine glands are ductless glands that pour their hormones directly into the blood.

stem: The hormone that controls metabolism and requires iodine is __________.
solution: Thyroxine from the thyroid gland controls metabolism and needs iodine for its production.

stem: Which of the following is TRUE about hormones?
options: They are secreted in small amounts and reach target organs through the blood
They are secreted in large amounts
solution: Hormones are secreted in tiny amounts and travel through the blood to their target organs.

stem: In insects like the frog, metamorphosis is controlled by hormones, showing that hormones also control __________ in animals.
solution: Hormones like thyroxine control metamorphosis in frogs, showing hormones control development in animals.

stem: Which of the following practices supports good health during adolescence?
options: Eating a balanced diet, exercising and maintaining hygiene
solution: A balanced diet, regular exercise and good hygiene support healthy development during adolescence.

stem: The age of marriage is legally set to protect health; in India, the legal minimum age for girls has traditionally been __________ years.
solution: The legal minimum marriage age for girls in India has traditionally been 18 years (and 21 for boys), to protect health.

stem: Why should adolescents not fall for advertisements promoting fairness creams or unhealthy body-image products?
options: Physical appearance changes are natural and such products can be misleading or harmful
solution: Body changes are natural; such products can be misleading, and self-worth should not depend on appearance.

stem: The reproductive phase of a woman's life, when she can bear children, is between __________.
solution: A woman can bear children between menarche (first menstruation) and menopause (its permanent stopping).

stem: Nutritious food during adolescence should include __________.
options: proteins, vitamins, minerals and adequate energy
solution: Adolescents need proteins for growth, plus vitamins, minerals (like iron and calcium) and enough energy.

stem: Which statement about the changes at adolescence is correct?
options: Different individuals may reach puberty at somewhat different ages
Everyone changes at exactly the same age
solution: The age and pace of pubertal changes vary from person to person, which is normal.

stem: The master gland that controls other endocrine glands is the __________.
solution: The pituitary gland controls the secretions of other endocrine glands and is called the master gland.

stem: A diet rich in iron during adolescence helps prevent __________, especially in girls.
solution: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin; adequate iron prevents anaemia, common in adolescent girls.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Reaching the Age of Adolescence' is that:
options: adolescence brings natural, hormone-controlled physical and mental changes leading to reproductive maturity, and requires good nutrition, hygiene and healthy choices
diet does not matter during adolescence
solution: The chapter explains the hormone-driven changes of adolescence and stresses balanced nutrition, personal hygiene and healthy, informed choices.
